text: Eye of the Storm (Japanese: , Tsumujikaze) is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Lone Exile class. Upon use, the user temporarily assumes defensive positions, during which attacks against them are blocked and countered with damage equal to 200% of their Attack, and any reactions are nullified.
Expansion Holders are Accessories in . They can be bought from the Nopon Coin X-change for 60 Silver Nopon Coins.
The Extra Provisions are a Key Item in . They are supplies dropped from Agnus Castle that the party retrieves for Colony Iota during Finite Time.
|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Expanding Memories are Accessories in . The legendary variant can be found from Wicked Wolf Aranqui.
Exxuno Bunnits are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Bunnit family, and can be found at level 21-24 on Yzana Plains and on Melnath's Shoulder.
Ether Spheres are a mechanic and special spots in , which begin to appear upon completing Champion of the Nopon.

Extended Slash (Japanese: , Ekusutendosurasshu) is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Yumsmith class. The Art inflicts the Shackle Blocking debuff, preventing affected enemies from guarding attacks. Additionally, the Art has increased effects when attacking from the front.

Evasive Posture is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Soulhacker class. It is acquired by defeating the Unique Monster Dishonest Karom while the Soul Hack skill is set on any player-controlled party member.
Evasion Down is a Status Effect in and . It reduces the affected character's evasion.

The Exile Fortress Ruins (Japanese: , Rutei no Torideato) is a Location in , located under Pioneer's Point on the Aurora Shelf. They are the ruins of the Exile Fortress from Satorl Marsh. The Unique Monster Radicalized Godwin and a Relic can be found here.

Ether Slides are a mode of transportation in . It is a green stream of Ether particles that characters can travel up and down on, similar to rails in the main game. However, the difference between the two is that Ether Slides can be utilized both ways, as compared to the rails' one-way travel. Ether Lifts are Ether Slides that go vertically. According to Panacea, Ether Slides were developed by Shulk and Riku.
Ether Lifts are a mode of transportation in . They are similar to Ether Slides, but allow the party to travel vertically.
Exquisite Bladestones are Key Items in . They can be found throughout the Cent-Omnia Region. They are used to upgrade the party's Blades to level VIII and level IX.

Ever Come to an End is a field track in , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda and sung by the Irish choir ANÚNA. This song plays during the day while the party is in Theosoir as well as at the Theosoir Rear Gate. It also plays throughout the Upper Level of the Kingdom of Tantal, including during battles, after the cutscene "Inherited Knowledge" is viewed and until the party enters Theosoir or Skip Travels to another Landmark. This song is one of the four songs from featured in ANÚNA's album "Otherworld". It is also featured as an available karaoke song in Karaoke JOYSOUND for Nintendo Switch.

Exploration is a track from , composed by ACE. It is track eight of disc one on the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track eight of disc six on the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays when the party engages an enemy in battle on the Ancient Ship, the Old Factory, and in the Spirit Crucible Elpys. This track also appears as a DLC music track in , included alongside Pyra and Mythra's Fighter Pack. It is a track option on Gaur Plain, the Cloud Sea of Alrest, Final Destination, and the three variants of Battlefield.
Ether Masts are objects in . They are Ether devices that give the location of any undiscovered points of interest within a certain area.

The FILE-SK-HRAESVELG is a Schematic in . This item is obtained as a reward for completing the Affinity Mission Thinking Makes It So. This schematic can be used to craft a level 60 Skell called Hraesvelg Lord at the AM Terminal.

Exhaust Hairs II are light head armour in . They can be obtained by winning with Sharla for the first time on the Battle Race course Twilight Speedway. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 3,800 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Sharla.

Exhaust Hairs I are light head armour in . They can be obtained by achieving a score of 2000 for the first time with Sharla in the Score Attack course Caterpile Circuit. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 2,500 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Sharla.

Exhaust Harnesses II are light torso armour in . They can be obtained by winning with Sharla for the first time on the Battle Race course Midnight Forest. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 6300 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Sharla.

Exhaust Harnesses I are light torso armour in . They can be obtained by achieving a score of 2200 for the first time with Sharla in the Score Attack course Jungle Rumble. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 4200 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Sharla.

Exhaust Tights II are light legs armour in . They can be obtained by winning with Sharla for the first time on the Battle Race course Blizzard Rally. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 4900 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Sharla.

Exhaust Tights I are light legs armour in . They can be obtained by achieving a score of 2600 for the first time with Sharla in the Score Attack course Valak Slalom. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 3300 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Sharla.

Exhaust Arms II are light arms armour in . They can be obtained by winning with Sharla for the first time on the Battle Race course Alcamoth at Dawn. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 2400 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Sharla.

Exhaust Arms I are light arms armour in . They can be obtained by achieving a score of 2400 for the first time with Sharla in the Score Attack course Alcamoth Orbital. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 1600 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Sharla.

Untamed Shoes II are light feet armour in . They can be obtained by winning with Sharla for the first time on the Battle Race course Colony 9 Wild Ride. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 4500 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Sharla.

Exhaust Boots I are light feet armour in . They can be obtained by achieving a score of 2800 for the first time with Sharla in the Score Attack course Rural Road. They can also be purchased from Time Attack for 3000 Noponstones. They can only be worn by Sharla.
Evanion is an NPC in . He is a Tantalese who can be found by Elmos Square in Theosoir in the Kingdom of Tantal.

Evasion is a stat in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Evasion is an effect allowing characters to dodge attacks. If a character's evasion is equal or greater than the opponent's accuracy, there is a maximum 95% chance of dodging attacks.

* F-Wave (GG) produced by Grenada Galactic Group resembles jet fighters. * F-Wave (ME) produced by Meredith & Co. resembles a series of blades on a rotor. * F-Wave (SA) produced by Sakuraba Industries resembles large discs.
Ether Resistance is a stat in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It displays resistance to ether-type attacks.
F2-Rifles are shoulder weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Ciniculas or Xe-doms.
F-Arrows are shoulder weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Caladars.
F-Grenades are shoulder weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Almandal, Millepods, Purgovents or Fuse Blower type Seidrs.
F-Rifles are shoulder weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Ciniculas or Xe-doms.

Fiora (Japanese: , Fiorun, Fiorung; English dub: ) is one of the seven playable characters in . She is a childhood friend of Shulk and Reyn, and is the younger sister of Dunban with whom she lives in his house in Colony 9. She has a soft spot for Shulk and often cooks for him, for which he is grateful. She becomes playable during Chapter 1 alongside Shulk and Reyn.

Financial Planning (Japanese: , Kōrigashi no Takurami) is a quest in . It can be received from King Squeeze northwest of the Commercial District of Colony 9. There are two routes that can be taken to complete this quest and An Impoverished Critic.

Fire Peppers (Japanese: , Faia Peppā) are collectables in . They can be found in Sword Valley and Colony 6. According to their description, they are so hot that someone who eats one will think they are on fire when they are actually on fire.
Fire Abrons (Japanese: , Faia Aburon) are collectables in . They can be found in the Ether Mine. According to their description, they are deep red statues of an unknown subject that Sharla named.

Fixing Time Mushrooms (Japanese: , Kinoko Tokei no Shūri) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Migaga at the Sacred Altar in Frontier Village. If Reyn is in the active party, he will comment. Migaga will give the party three lots of Compost upon accepting the quest.
The Fallen Arm Collection is a portion of the Collectopaedia in .

This quest will expire after the events at the Mechonis Core. Find the Kingpin (Japanese: , Kuromaku wo Sagase) is a Timed Quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Gadada after completing Dangerous Ambition. He can be found in the Pollen Works in Frontier Village. In order to complete this quest, Secret Mission must also be completed. If Riki is in the active party, he will comment.

Fire Tarantulas (Japanese: , Moetaranchura) are collectables in . They are extremely rare, and can be found on Bionis' Leg. According to their description, they are adorable tarantulas whose many hairs are deadly poisonous.

Feather Leaves (Japanese: , Fezāzu Rīfu) are collectables in . They can be found in Satorl Marsh. According to their description, they are furry leaves mainly used for bedclothes. Four are required for Making Camp.

Field Ponios are enemies in . They are members of the Ponio family, and can be found at level 12-14 in the eastern end of Gaur Plain on Bionis' Leg, around the trees near Kamos Guidepost. They are usually found alongside Niece Ponios. Five of them need to be defeated for Bionis' Leg's Monster Quest 1 - Part 3. They can drop the Ponio Neck Meat needed for A Thoughtful Idea.

Fancy Bolts (Japanese: , Fanshī Boruto) are collectables in . They can be found in Agniratha and later in Colony 6. According to their description, they are bolts with strangely pretty heads and tightening them looks like fun.

Fairy Tale Diodes (Japanese: , Meruhen Daiōdo) are collectables in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found in Agniratha and later in Colony 6. According to their description, it is said that gazing into the red light can trap someone in an enchanted world. Five are required for Agniratha Beautification 1.
Field Shoes are light feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be bought from the shop at the Refugee Camp Shop on Bionis' Leg for 2,400 G.
Field Caps (Japanese: , Fīrudo Kyappu) are light head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be obtained through trading.
Field Bottoms are light legs armour in . They can only be obtained through trading.
Field Tops are light torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be obtained by trading.

Faras Cave (Japanese: , Farasu no Kyōkai Izumi) is a Secret Area in . It is a small cave in the Eryth Sea, located south of Hovering Reef 9. Twelve collectable orbs can be found here at night. When collecting these orbs it has been found that at least one will usually be a Night Lily, while the others are random items on the Eryth Sea collection list.
Firing Hammers (Japanese: , Gekitetsu) are weapons in . They are Dunban's swords, and can be dropped by the Hover Astas.
Fixing a Broken Door (Japanese: , Kowareta Doa no Shūri) is a quest in . It is received by Rizaka in the Hidden Machina Village on the Fallen Arm. If Reyn is in the active party, he will comment.

Fine Fliers (Japanese: , Fain Furaia) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Flier family, and can be found at level 12 in Gaur Plain on Bionis' Leg. They can drop the Flier Straws needed for A Gutsy Trader.

Fish Biters (Japanese: , Aozakana no Kamukamu) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Biters wielded by Riki, and can be dropped by various enemies or traded for with one NPC. They cannot be bought or obtained as a quest reward.
Final Cut (Japanese: , Fainarukatto) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are twin blades wielded by Fiora, and can only be acquired from a chest inside the Giant's ruins on Three Sage Summit.
Falcon Blades (Japanese: , Hayabusa Sōken) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are twin blades wielded by Fiora, and can only be acquired from one shop, in Colony 6.

Filtered Water is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is found at the Sparkling Pool in Makna Forest from dawn to dusk. The party is asked by Rasha to give it to Cherri during the Secret Innovation.
The Family Picture is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be found near the Fountain of Hope in Alcamoth. Atael asks the party to collect it during A Memento of Daddy.

Firework Geldesia (Japanese: , Hibana no Gerudeshia) is a quest exclusive Unique Monster in . It is a Queen member of the Arachno family. It can be found at level 98 at the Arachno Queen's Nest in Tephra Cave during Battling Brutes and after the events at Mechonis Core (Chapter 17), facing its nemesis, the Reckless Zanden, a gigantic Gogol.

Final Challenge of the Sage (Japanese: , Sennin no Saishū Shiren) is a quest in . It can be received from the Nopon Sage in Makna Forest after clearing the Mechonis Core. Nopon Sage lies at the Ether Crystal Deposit area north of the Divine Sanctuary and southwest of Waypoint Beacon, from 12:00 to 15:00. He will only give the quest to Riki. After completing the quest, Riki's fifth skill branch, Heroism, will be unlocked.

Fertile Flamii Eggs are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Flamiis on the Bionis' Leg or traded for. According to their description, they are eggs with a foul taste that is disliked by predators, so they always hatch. Two are required for Material Quest 1 (Bionis' Leg).

The Fiendish Bunnit (Japanese: , Akugyaku no Banitto) is a quest exclusive enemy in . It is a member of the Bunnit family. It is found near a cliff area east of Cliff Lake in Colony 9 during Pestering Paola.

Falsel Bunnivs (Japanese: , Faruseru Banīvu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Bunniv family, and can be found at level 91-93 near the Heavenly Window in Tephra Cave. They can drop the Bunniv Clubs needed for Friendship Tokens.

Fascia Bunnivs (Japanese: , Fashia Banīvu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Bunniv family. They can be found in the Heavenly Window in Tephra Cave at level 92-94. Can easily be respawned by skip traveling to Heavenly Window. It can drop the Bunniv Clubs needed for Friendship Tokens. It is one of the few respawnable enemies that drops the Ether Drain Battle Art book, but with a 2.1% drop rate it has the lowest drop rate of any item this enemy carries. It is suggested to kill the monster until it drops a gold chest, then save. After the save, open the chest. If the Ether Drain book is not there, reload and kill the monster again, and if it drops another gold chest s

Fancy Orluga Masks are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Orlugas in Makna Forest or traded for in Frontier Village. According to their description, although they are used for soothing babies, it is quite scary to see them suddenly. Five are needed for Material Quest 2 (Frontier Village).
Fine Parts L are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from M88/WORST and M96/AWAKE in the Central Factory. They are not otherwise available.
Fine Parts S are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from various Mechon in the Central Factory. They are not available otherwise.

Fair Piranhax (Japanese: , Fea Samon) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Piranhax family, and can be found at level 54 on the Fallen Arm, at the Radiocarpea Coast or the Inlet Beach. They are the only sources of Piranhax Fishmeals, five of them which are needed for Colony 6 Reconstruction to complete Level 4 Commerce.
First Attack Plus (Japanese: , Kaimaku Kōgeki Kyōka) is a Gem in that increases Damage on the first attack of combat. __TOC__
Fall Defence (Japanese: , Rakka Bōgyo) is a Gem in that reduces damage taken from falling. __TOC__

Field Altrich (Japanese: , Nakahara no Orutoritchi) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Tirkin family, and can be found at level 76 northwest of Crevasse Waterfall on Bionis' Leg, accompanied by a group of significantly weaker Tirkin. It can drop Tirkin Elder Medals, one of which required for the quest Replica Monado 4. It is the strongest Tirkin in the game.
Faithful Lancelot (Japanese: , Shinkō no Ransurotto) is a Unique Monster in . It can be found at level 59 in the Central Factory right next to the Control Tower.

Feris (Japanese: , Ferisu, lit. Felis, Felid) are large cat-like enemies in the . These creatures are most likely to be based on lions and leopards, hence the name derived from feline. Feris undergo a massive appearance change between games; in and , they resemble spotted lions with large, spiked manes. In , , and they retain the mane but otherwise are completely different - they are brown with red hair and dog-like, with long muzzles and bushy tails. In they are paler with orange hair.
Final Flicker (Japanese: , Haisui Eigi) is one of Dunban's supporting arts in . It sacrifices 20% of his max HP to fill 50% of his Talent Gauge.

Fiora's Conviction (Japanese: , Fiorun no Settoku) is a Story Quest in . It is received automatically while progressing through Galahad Fortress, at Face Maintenance Bay taking a lift down from the Preparation Bay. This story quest is related to a story battle event involving Fiora as Face Nemesis defended by four security Mechon, the two Defensive Guard Units and the two M94 Guard Units.

Final Cross (Japanese: , Fainaru Kurosu) is one of Fiora's Ether arts in . Fiora learns this art after defeating Gadolt for the last time. Final Cross is a frontal area Ether attack that unleashes a massive Ether wave and hits targets four times. Successful attacks force Topple on targets. This art can only be used when Fiora's tension is very high.

Family Secrets (Japanese: , Chichi ni Kakurete, Hiding from Father) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Zel Argentis in Colony 6. Betrothal Test can be triggered after completing this quest. This quest is mutually exclusive with Family Secrets involving En Argentis, whose invitation to Colony 6 is mutually exclusive. If Sharla is in the active party, she will comment.

Feris Blood is a rare material in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be dropped by Feris in Makna Forest or traded for. According to their description, they are red drinks that are loved by all connoisseurs for their nice sharpness and flavour. Two are needed for Losing the Taste for Alcohol.
Fighter Ignas are enemies in . They are members of the Igna family, and can be found at level 27 NE of Crown Tree, near Zaldania Waterfall, and in Igna Territory in Satorl Marsh.
Fate Labolas (Japanese: , Unmei no Raborasu) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a Mechon, and can be found at level 51 in the Port Maintenance Bay in Sword Valley.

Fierce Vang (Japanese: , Mōkō no Vanpu) are five bat-like quest exclusive enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Vang family, and can be found in Kisk Cave on Bionis' Leg only during the Earnest's Fibs quest. They will drop Vang Third Molars needed for Material Quest 4.

Ferocious Volffs (Japanese: , Mōgeki no Vorufu) are quest exclusive enemies in . They are members of the Volff family, and can be found at level 12 on Bionis' Leg near a small waterfall between the Jabos Rock Rest Area and the Volff Lair. Ferocious Volff only appear during the surprise quest Save the Girl!, which requires that the party defeat them.

Fiora's Treatment (Japanese: , Fiorun no Chiryō) is a Story Quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. This quest is given by Linada, shortly after the story event triggered once the party met Miqol and ended by the party talking with her in the Junks at the Hidden Machina Village on the Fallen Arm.

Fiery Ignas (Japanese: , Kasei no Igūna) are quest exclusive enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Igna family, and can be found at level 37 near the Freight Road in Colony 6 only during the quest Defend Colony 6 - Reptile. To complete the quest, five Fiery Ignas must be defeated.

Fancy Volff Hides are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from various Volff in Satorl Marsh. Fancy Volff Hides are also available via trade with Zazadan or with Kacha via overtrade. According to their description, they are resplendent VIP pelts and wearing one is considered using the royal we. Three Fancy Volff Hides are needed for Making Camp.

Finding the Unfindable (Japanese: , Komarihateta Nandemoya) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Shilx lying on upstairs near the Main Entrance in Colony 6. If Reyn is in the active party, he will comment.

Fallen Objects are two Key Items in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are needed to complete Presents for Priceless Pupils. One can be found on the northwest shore from Anti-Air Battery 2. The other is on the small platform just below the cannon itself, and immediately south of the label for Anti-Air Battery 2 on the map screen.

The First Lung (Japanese: , Dai 1 Hai Naibu) is a location in , and is one of Bionis' three lungs. It is located in the Bionis' Interior, accessible from the Interior Landing Site. It leads out to the Spinal Nerve Tower. There is a Rank V water Ether Crystal deposit here containing Aura Heal V and Aquatic Cloak V crystals.

Find a Path to the Top (Japanese: , Jōsō e no Michi wo Sagase) is a Story Quest in . It is received automatically while leaving the Central Warehouse Lift in Central Factory. During the second objective, upon arrival at the Factory Vent, the story quest Materials for a Bomb is automatically triggered.
This page is a list of all the Unique Monsters on the Fallen Arm.
The Factory Vent (Japanese: , Seisan Kōjō Tsūfūkō) is a landmark in . It is located on the second floor of the Central Factory, near the Main Factory Gate.

The Factory Transporter (Japanese: , Chūō Kōshō Iki Ten'i Sōchi) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is located on the ground floor of Agniratha, near the Cleas Pillar. It is a transporter connecting to the Agniratha Transporter in the Central Factory.
Fatty Sardi Meats are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from Mellow Sardi on Bionis' Leg. Fatty Sardi Meats are also available via trade.
Firm Skin is a common material in . It is dropped by Heavy Brogs. No one has it available for trade.
Fine Parts M are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from various Mechon in the Central Factory. They are not available for purchase or trade.

Fiora's Cooking (Japanese: , Fiorun no Teryōri, Fiora's Home Cooking) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located in Dunban's House in Colony 9, between Reyn and Fiora at green affinity. It can only be viewed after the Mechon attack on the colony.

Fallen Brethren (Japanese: , Kyoshin ni Kaetta Monotachi e, For Those Returned to the Bionis) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located by the Agni Tablet in Makna Forest, between Shulk and Melia at green affinity.
Fiora's Body (Japanese: , Fiorun no Karada) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located just south of the Spinal Nerve Tower in the Bionis' Interior, between Fiora and Sharla at pink affinity.

The Fixed Pendant is a Key Item in . It belongs to Sonia and is a memento of her dead husband. It is received from Dean when he fixes the Broken Pendant as part of Rocco's Heartful Request, and is to be returned to Rocco.
The Fixed Toy is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is received from Satata during Being A Good Grandfather and must be delivered to his grandson, Kiroki.

Fire Carnival is a Ranged Art and one of Lin's two Signature Arts in . Cross can learn this art after completing the mission The Repair Job. In the attack, the wielder's Gatling Gun deploys a hidden missile launcher and fires a barrage of micro-missiles at the target.

fiKAIeldJOU is a track in Xenoblade Chronicles X, composed and arranged by Hiroyuki Sawano. It is track seven of disc three from the XenobladeX Original Soundtrack. This music is heard while the party is in the water regions of Mira.

Falsaxum (Japanese: , Garukasu) are large, rocky beetle-like creatures in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They somewhat look like a rock turtle but are Insectoids. They can be found in Noctilum, Oblivia, and Sylvalum. They are counterparts of Ciniculas.

Fernando, the Immovable (Japanese: , Fudō no Ferunando) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Millesaur family. It can be found at level 85 in Noctilum at the Decapotamon during the day.

Fighter Grexes (Japanese: , Faitā Rupusu) are six Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Grexes and can be found at level 12 on Biahno Grassland in Primordia. They appear and accompany the Sailing Grex during A Day in the Life.

The Fierce Vigent (Japanese: , Fīsu Pekkā) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Vigent family. It is fought at level 19 in the clearing south of the Leaning Ring in Oblivia during A Friend in Need.

Fighter Pugiliths (Japanese: , Faitā Berudero) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Pugilith machines, Ganglion's vehicles, and can be found at levels 21-30 in Noctilum. One can be found at level 24 at the Lotus Keep Building Site, one hex northwest of FN Site 210. They drop New Cylinders, two of which are needed for Skell Repair: Cylinder and It's-a Mia!. They are lower level than the Guardian Pugiliths mentioned in the mission's objectives as a source for New Cylinders.

Fighter Puges (Japanese: , Faitā Berude) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Puge machines, Ganglion's human size robots, and can be found at level 21 or 26 in Cauldros's White Phosphor Lake.
Finishing Blow is a Soul Voice in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is triggered when a party member deals a finishing blow to an enemy.

Fell Terebras (Japanese: , Fōru Rutoru, Fall Lutru) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Terebra family. They can be found at level 51-52 in Primordia at Northpointe Beach and FN Site 111.

Fearsome Ictuses (Japanese: , Fiā Manda, Fear Manda) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Ictus family, and can be found at level 41-44 in the Alexander Ridge or near Victory Rock in Oblivia. Five must be defeated to complete Arms Testers Wanted.

The Falconine Jacul (Japanese: , Īguru Hasutara, Eagle Jacul) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Contary to its name, it is an Auravis. It is fought at level 29 at Keegan Ridge in Oblivia during Mighty Mia.

Factory 1.21 (Japanese: , Fakutorī 1.21) is a commercial Arms Manufacturer in Xenoblade Chronicles X. The CEO is Professor B, an individual dealer with unique taste. He has a large following of quiet, but extremely loyal, customers. This AM is unlocked upon completion of the Normal Mission Professor B's Return. He produces rare and valuable gravity-attribute products. Known for attention to detail in both form and function. Factory 1.21 does not produce armor.

Ferdinand, the Fortuitous (Japanese: , Kyōun no Ferudinan) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Mephite family. It can be found at level 28 near Lake Basel in Oblivia, next to a sitting Canyon Sylooth southwest of Dorian Caravan. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Ferdinand, the Fortuitous. It is the target of one of the Squad Tasks for Squad Mission No.7.
Fitting In (Japanese: , Shinwa, Friendship) is an Affinity Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be accepted near the Outfitters Test Hangar in the Industrial District.
Fathers and Sons (Japanese: , Oya to Ko, Parent and Child) is an Affinity Mission in . It can be accepted in the BLADE Barracks in New Los Angeles.
False Cedars (Japanese: , Masukesugi) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum.

False Thalluses (Japanese: , Feiku Arudare) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Thallus family. They can be found at level 21-30 in Noctilum, near FN Site 225 as well as in the tunnel between Dead Man's Ingress and Dead Man's Gulch. Defeating three of them is required during Thinning the Thalluses (False).

Faded Thalluses (Japanese: , Fēdo Arudare) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Thallus family. They can be found at level 32-34 in Oblivia at FN Site 308. Some sit in the sand while some sit on the rock wall. They drop Red Thallus Antennae, two of which are needed for the Normal Mission Emotion Commotion.
Fillal Filths (Japanese: , Firuero no Kuso) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia, in particular north of Arendt Bridge.

Facewoods (Japanese: , Feisuuddo) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found rarely in Primordia, around the entrance of Castaway Cavern, usually around the poisonous pool where a Treasure Box sits.

Fallshorn Isle (Japanese: , Rōdansō no Shima) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a cliff located in Primordia, southwest of Biahno Grassland and northeast of Headwater Summit. The FN Site 106 is located here, and it must be visited during Then and Now.
Fine Black Belts are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Prone and Definians.
Fine Duoguill Fishmeals are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Duoguills.
Felice is an NPC in . She can be found at the Nopon Bazaar in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles.

Feliciano, the All-Seeing (Japanese: , Shingan no Ferishiano) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Sphinx family. It can be found at level 70 at the Central Ibra Ravine in Oblivia during the day. It has a counter spike that inflicts physical attribute damage as well as Physical Res Down VI; it does not activate until Feliciano, the All-Seeing has engaged in battle.

Femme Forfexes (Japanese: , Famu Pagurusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Forfex family, and can be found at level 28-29 at FN Site 115 in Primordia during rainy weather.

Falchion, the Vibrant (, Senretsu no Farushion) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Cinicula family. It can be found at level 30 under an arch near FN Site 208 in Noctilum, where it emerges from the ground.

Feld, the Indigo-Clad (Japanese: , Hanadaodoshi no Ferudo) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Turba family. It can be found at level 31 at the Secluded Lava Lake in Sylvalum, which can be found in a cave right next to the FN Site 401.

Filiavents (Japanese: , Nagwada) are huge Piscinoid enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They resemble sea anemones; their bodies can extend to great heights during battle, and they can hover slightly off the ground. They can be found in Noctilum, Sylvalum, and Cauldros. During battles, filliavents primarily use electric-based attacks.

Fiendish Viragos (Japanese: , Fīndo Toruto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Virago family, and can be found at level 44-50 at Qing Long Glade in Noctilum during the day. Three must be defeated during Arms Testers Wanted.

Fiasco Saltats (Japanese: , Rūzā Sarutāto, Loser Saltat) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Saltat family, and can be found at level 31-40 at Scholes Battlegrounds in Cauldros during clear weather, rarely replacing the Strange Saltats that appear there.
Fine White Belts are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Marnucks in Sylvalum.
Fast Forward is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Galactic Knight at rank 5.
Feather Touch is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Psycorruptor at rank 8. Cross, Irina, and Celica can use this skill.
Feloran (Japanese: , Ferōran) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are a Zaruboggan and can be found at the Starboard of the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles.
Fell Fashion is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from Candid & Credible and the primary destination is Sylvalum.
Fine Red Belts are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Marnucks in Cauldros.
Filiavent Intestines are intergalactic materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Filiavents. They are components in X, XV, and XX Fuel Efficiency Up augments.
Fending Off Forfexes is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from the Interceptors and the primary destination is Noctilum.

The Faded Nopopotamus (Japanese: , Feido Nopohippo) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a tame Potamus that is used by Nopon as a beast of burden, carrying a large bundle of packages on its back. It is fought at level 17 in the Den of the Dead in Sylvalum during Special Delivery.

Facts and Feelings is Doug's first Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is available if Doug's affinity is at 1♥ and a dog is selected as the pet in the BLADE Barracks, and occurs in the afternoon in the Residential District's Ishmael Hills.
Filter Testing is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Despite what the mission states, Transparent Membranes can drop from any Unafulge on Mira.

Find My Doc! is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from Jalimbo and the primary destination is the Residential District. It leads into Rites of Ruin, though accepting this mission is not a prerequisite.
Find the Freighter is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from Roscoe and the primary destination is the Industrial District of New Los Angeles.
Finding Morrows Today is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a botanist and the primary destination is Noctilum.

Field-Skill is a stat in . Upgrading Field-Skills is needed to be able to open treasures and install Data Probes that require a higher Field-Skill than level 1. There are three types of Field-Skills: * Archaeological * Biological * Mechanical Field Skills can be upgraded by speaking to Eleonora after increasing the player's BLADE Level. For every BLADE Level up, she will upgrade one Field-Skill of the player's choice. However, she can only upgrade a Field-Skill to a maximum of level 4. To upgrade Field-Skills to level 5, the three mechanical, archaeological and biological Off the Record Basic Missions must be completed. There are three different types of treasures that can be found throughou
Fight Scrubs is a Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located southeast of Central Melville Street in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles between the Murderess and Cross at night.
Far from Home is a Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located at the Outfitters Test Hangar (on the roof) in the Industrial District of New Los Angeles between Celica and Cross at night.

Falsaxum Shells are rare materials in . They can be obtained from Falsaxum, for 90 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks, or for 30 Material Tickets from the Material Market in . They are a component of I and V Physical Res Up and SpecUp.PHYS-RES augments.

Fal-swo Solar Crests are rare materials in . They can be obtained from Fal-swos, for 90 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks, or for 35 Material Tickets from the Material Market in . They are a component of I and V Evasion Boost and Boost.EVA augments.

Fertilized Jacul Eggs are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Jaculs, or for 90 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are a component of X, XV, and XX Overdrive Count Up and Overdrive.EXTEND augments.

Fine Aprica Wood are unique materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Apricas, or for 114 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components for I, V, and X Overdrive Surge augments. Two are needed for From Idea to Inventory.

Fine Transparent Belts are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from certain Marnucks, or for 26 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components for I and V Bind: Refuel augments.
Femina Suid A is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a red female suid variant. It can be obtained from Melanya, the Sound Sleeper in Oblivia.
Femina Suid B is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a pale brown female suid variant. It can be obtained from Manuelita, the Affectionate in Noctilum.
Falsaxum A is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a brown falsaxum variant. It can be obtained from Clemente, the Iron Meteor in Noctilum.
Falsaxum B is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a white and green falsaxum variant. It can be obtained from Mikulas, the Keystone in Sylvalum.
Filiavent A is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a red filiavent variant. It can be obtained from Laurencio, the Fog Bow in Sylvalum.
Filiavent B is a Holofigure in . It depicts a black filiavent variant. It can be obtained from Trueno, the Cataclysm in Cauldros.
Fal-swo A is a Holofigure in . It can be obtained from Ji-ett, the Thunderclap in Primordia.
Fal-swo B is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be obtained from Ya-rhat, the Thundercloud in Cauldros.
Fal-swo C is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be obtained from No-dhor, the Shadowcaster in Oblivia.
Fal-swo D is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a silver fal-swo variant with light green lights. It can be obtained from Ga-uhl, the Precept-Keeper in Sylvalum.

Feeding Ground Clash is a Squad Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is part of BLADE Mission No.6, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting eighteen Terebras. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Fell the Giant Grex is a Squad Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is part of BLADE Mission No.9, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting twenty-two Saltats. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Fish in Troubled Waters is a Squad Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is part of BLADE Mission No.13, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting twenty Mechanoids. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.
Firing Range Up is a ground weapon mod Augment in and that increases the firing range for ranged weapons. It can only be equipped on ranged weapons. The Skell equivalent is Custom.WP-R-RANGE.

The First Barrier Key is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It must be obtained along with the Second and Third Barrier Keys to lower a forcefield during Definian Downfall. It is dropped by the Milsaadi Guard at the entrance to the southeast room of the Ganglion Antropolis in Cauldros.
Fatigue is a stat debuff in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Fatigue reduces damage dealt by melee Auto-Attacks and Battle Arts.
Fireguns are sidearms for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Colubrims or Oc-servs.
Faithful Glaives are melee weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Longswords. They can be obtained from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 18,000 Credits.
Faithful Glaives II are melee weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Longswords. They can be obtained from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 27,000 Credits.
Faithful Lances are melee weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Javelins. They can be obtained from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 23,400 Credits.
Faithful Edges are melee weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Dual Swords in the Edges Series. They can be obtained from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 16,200 Credits.
Faithful Edges II are melee weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Dual Swords in the Edges Series. They can be obtained from the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley for 16,200 Credits.
Fatty Fish Bellies are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from Fair Piranhax on the Fallen Arm. Fatty Fish Bellies are also available via trade.

Field Armus (Japanese: , Fīrudo Aruma) are enemies in . They are members of the Armu family and can be found at level 3 - 11 on the Upper Level - Right area of Gormott Province, particularly on Garanti Plain or at Lyta Oasis. They do not appear during thunderstorms.

Fishy Fishy (Japanese: , Sakanaya Pitchipitchi) is a shop in . It is run by Kitoto and can be found at Rumbletum Canteen in Goldmouth in the Argentum Trade Guild. It is specialized in Seafood. Store Deeds can be purchased after buying at least one of each item from the shop.
Feral Blade (Japanese: , Wairudoejji, Lit. "Wild Edge") is a Driver Art in It is one of Rex's arts when using a Chroma Katana.
Feral Spin (Japanese: , Wairudosupin, Lit. "Wild Spin") is a Driver Art in . It is one of Rex's arts when using a Megalance.
Falcon Turn (Japanese: , Farukontān) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Nia's arts when using a Bitball. In the , it is also one of Nia's arts when using Bunnie.
Feral Uppercut (Japanese: , Wairudoappā, Lit. "Wild Upper") is a Driver Art in . It is one of Rex's arts when using Knuckle Claws.
The First Low Orbit Station (Japanese: , Daiichi teikidō sutēshon), Rhadamanthus, is the final region in .

Final Choruses are Art Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Maluria Antiques in Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya and from Jugos Antiques in the Indoline Praetorium. They are one of the favorite Pouch items of Mythra. Two need to be used to unlock Mythra's Level 3 "Focus" Field Skill.
The Factory Catwalk (Japanese: , Haikōjō Barukonī) is a Landmark in . It is located at the entrance to the Old Factory in the Empire of Mor Ardain.

Farlaine Wells (Japanese: , Fāren Suiiki) is a location in . It is located in the Stomach of the Kingdom of Uraya. This place makes up most of the northern part of the Stomach and is mostly shallow water. A cave at the northernmost point leads into the Cataracts of Rujah and the Farlaine Central Pools can be found to the south.

The Farlaine Central Pools (Japanese: , Fāren Chūō Kadan-gun) are a Location in . They are located in the Stomach of the Kingdom of Uraya, around Yurna the Elderwood. Directly north is the Farlaine Wells, and walkways from here lead up to Minnet Terrace and Pelza's Sluice. A jump point in the water requiring Level 2 "Wind Mastery" and "Leaping" Field Skills leads up to a treetop containing the Heart-to-heart "Tora's Angst". Ragi can be found here before Gotta Start Somewhere!.

The Fallen-Down Pilgrim's Way (Japanese: , Hōrakushita Junreiro) is a location in . It is located on the Upper Level of the Cliffs of Morytha, between the Path of the Believer and Balquors Ruins. It is a series of torch-lit wooden platforms that must be jumped between. There are no enemies here.

The Fallen Skyscraper (Japanese: , Taoreta Ofisubiru) is a landmark in . It is located on the Streets of the Land of Morytha, beyond the Blocked Road. It can be climbed to access Highway 8. The Golden Sunstone can be found here.
The Fishy Fishy Deeds are Store Deeds in . They can be purchased from Fishy Fishy in the Argentum Trade Guild after purchasing every Pouch Item sold there.

Fish and Herb Broths are Seafood Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Hanoon Fishmongers in Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain. They are one of the favorite Pouch items of Agate. They can also be purchased for 2,520 G from the Pouch Item Emporium in the Land of Challenge after collecting the Nopon Invitation, Pt. 2 on Version 1.5.2 or later.
Felmeri Fairy Statues are Art Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Yafush Antiques in Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain. They are one of the favorite Pouch items of Kasandra.
Fizzy Lassis are Drink Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Vargel Tavern in Garfont Village in the Kingdom of Uraya.
The Fallone Deeds are a Store Deed key item in . They can be purchased from Fallone Crafts in Garfont Village in the Kingdom of Uraya.
Fallone Crafts is a shop in . It is run by Lavvade and can be found in Garfont Village in the Kingdom of Uraya. It is specialized in Textiles.

Field Arduns (Japanese: , Fīrudo Arudon) are enemies in . They are members of the Ardun family and can be found at level 5-13 on the upper right level of the Gormott Province, particularly on Garanti Plain or at Lyta Oasis. They do not appear during thunderstorms.

Faros Ignas (Japanese: , Farosu Igūna) are enemies in . They are Ignas and can be found at level 78-80 in Badfella's Cave Fort in the Stomach of the Kingdom of Uraya. They are the only Ignas in Uraya that fight while riding another creature, as they ride Rhinons.

Femni Nests (Japanese: , Femunī Nesuto) are enemies in . They are Nests that can be found in the Stomach of the Kingdom of Uraya, particularly at level 38 around Fonsa Myma Waters or level 42-45 in the Old Quarry.
Fiar Garluses (Japanese: , Fīaru Garuusu) are enemies in . They are members of the Garlus family, and can be found at level 37-43 on Lumos Pillar on the Upper Level of the Kingdom of Tantal.
Fend Vangs (Japanese: , Fendā Vanpu) are enemies in . They are members of the Vang family, and can be found at level 79-84 at Heimos's Crevasse on the Lower Level of the Kingdom of Tantal.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Fiber Hats (Japanese: , Faibā Hatto) are accessories in . They increase the wearer's Ether stat by up to 32%. They are the upgraded version of the Bolt Hat and Pearl Hat. The DLC exclusive Prairie Cap accessory offers a stronger instance of this equipment's effect. For a similar additive effect that can stack with this gear, check the Fluffy Hat and Fabulous Hat accessories.

Fang Chips are Core Chips in and . They can be purchased from Zelkova Blacksmiths in Torigoth, and Lascham Weapons in Lascham Cove, and have no other sources. Fang Chips share their appearance with Horn Chips, Scale Chips, and Wing Chips. __TOC__

False Rumor is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Empire of Mor Ardain during the Blade Quest Crystal Clear, after talking to Iannus. The time required to complete this mission is 20 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 5 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Girls' Talk" and "Expeditionist" Field Skills.
Fairy-Tale Belt Pullies are Mechanical collectibles in . They can be found in the Leftherian Archipelago, in particular by Salvaging on Daram Isle.
Fan Skinks are Insect collectibles in . They can be found in the Empire of Mor Ardain. In the , Fsn Skinks can also be obtained by scanning an amiibo.
Firering Radishes are Vegetable collectibles in . They can be found at the Cliffs of Morytha.
Fast Twitch (Japanese: , Kuikkumassuru, Lit. "Quick Muscle") is a Driver Art in . It is one of Vandham's arts when using the Dual Scythes.

First Mission is a Merc Mission in . It is received during the course of Vandham's Last Wish. As the name implies, it is the first Merc Mission given to the party. The time required to complete this mission is 1 minute. Despite suggesting the "Transport Mastery", "Industry Mastery" and "Production Mastery" Field Skills for the task, the duration of the mission cannot be lowered further.

Felt Cushionings are Textile Pouch items in . They can be made by Vale using her "Weaving Lv.2" field skill at Vale's Weaving in Fonsett Village, Leftheria. They are unlocked when Vale attains Weaving Lv.2 by making 10 fabrics.
Falc Lexos (Japanese: , Faruke Rekusosu) are enemies in . They are members of the Lexos family and can be found at level 43-46 on Baldotas Isle in the Leftherian Archipelago.

Figgle Drivers (Japanese: , Fōgeru Doraibā) are enemies in . They are human Drivers, and can be found at level 97 in the Old Factory in the Empire of Mor Ardain after reaching the First Low Orbit Station.

Familion Sovereigns (Japanese: , Fōmyurā Roiyaru) are enemies in . They are Familion-type Sovereigns that can be found at level 56-64 north of the Sky Bridge or at the Mizar, Elevator #8 on the Lower Level of the World Tree. Some of them can be summoned at level 54-56 by Gerolf Sovereign, Grandum Sovereign, Skriim Sovereign by using their art "Eject Rider", at level 55-57 by Mk. VI Margot by using its art "Transfer Gate"; at level 65 by Mk. VI Gerolf by using its art "Eject Rider", or at level 99 by the Gerolf Sovereigns summoned by Mk. VII Arek by using its art "Eject Rider". Four of them (or Sting Runners) must be defeated to unlock Herald and Akhos' level 3 "Electric Mastery".

Felusi Pippitos (Japanese: , Ferūze Pipitto) are enemies in . They are members of the Pippito family, and can be found at level 58-60 at the Control Room and the 7th Perimeter Skyport in the World Tree.

Fissa Aligos (Japanese: , Fisshā Diburo) are enemies in . They are members of the Aligo family, and can be found at level 33-37 at the Salvage Points of Triedge Isle and Battlescar Cove in Temperantia.
Feyla is an NPC in . Feyla is a Gormotti who can be found in the Grodd Residential Zone of Torigoth in the Gormott Province. Feyla gives the quest The Missing Order.
Ferrii Aligos (Japanese: , Feirī Diburo) are enemies in . They are members of the Aligo family, and can be found at level 38-42 after Salvaging at Goetuis Wharf #1 in the Indoline Praetorium.

Farewell, Good Friend is a quest in . It is received by Farraw in the Ayvill Shopping District of the Empire of Mor Ardain. After this quest is completed, high-level enemies such as Beast-Hunter William will appear in the Olethro Playhouse. This quest will be available once Insurgent Investigations has been completed.
Farraw is an NPC in . She is an Ardainian who can be found in the Ayvill Shopping District in the Empire of Mor Ardain. She proposes the quest Farewell, Good Friend.
The Filament Globe is a Key Item in . It is obtained as a reward after completing the quest Tirkin Suppression given by Saclich after approaching the Salvage Point in the Torigoth Relay Base.

The Firan Driver (Japanese: , Firan Doraibā) is a quest-exclusive boss in . He is a Driver enemy who is fought at level 45 at the Fonsa Myma Port in the Kingdom of Uraya during Theory and Praxis, alongside the Avarr Driver and Torst Drivers.

|-|Aux Core = |-|Skill RAM/Upgrade = Fire Absorb (Japanese: , Hi Zokusei Kyūshū Shīrudo) is an Aux Core or a Skill RAM/Upgrade in . Every time the user blocks a Fire elemental attack, this equipment nullifies the damage taken and converts it into HP restoration. The Skill RAM/Upgrade variants can be used to customize Poppi α, Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ as an Aux Core equivalent. __TOC__
The Favored Hammer is a Key Item in . It is obtained from Tonadon at the Goldmouth Wheelhouse in the Argentum Trade Guild if Floren is in the party and has level 1 "Beguiling Charms".

The Fizz Contract is a Key Item in . It is received as a reward after completing the Merc Mission Fad Foods. It enables the purchase of Fizzy Lassi from the Vargel Tavern shop at Garfont Village in the Kingdom of Uraya.

The Felmeri Contract is a Key Item in . It is received as a reward after completing the Merc Mission Secret Spice. It enables the purchase of Felmeri Fairy Statue from the Yafush Antiques shop at Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain.

The Fish Contract is a Key Item in . It is received as a reward after completing the Merc Mission Cold Storage. It enables the purchase of Fish and Herb Broths from the Hanoon Fishmongers shop at Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain.

Find Akatsuki is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Empire of Mor Ardain during the quest Insurgent Investigations. The time required to complete this mission is 30 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 7 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Fortitude", "Info Collector" and "Expeditionist" Field Skills.

Fake Vase is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Tantal automatically after completing the Blade Quest Failure and Success. The time required to complete this mission is 20 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 5 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Dark Mastery", "Assassination" and "Leaping" Field Skills. Completing this mission unlocks the Merc Mission Beautiful Flower.
Final Stone (Japanese: , Rokkusurasuto, Lit. "Rock Thrust") is a Driver Art in . It is one of Rex's arts when using a Cobra Bardiche. This art recycles Rex's Heavy Hitter.

Falling Dropkick (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Zeke's arts when using Rockrending Gauntlets. It can be obtained upon New Game Plus, after finishing the game and installing Patch (Ver.1.3.0). This art recycles Zeke's Fury Dropkick.

The Fire Dragons Members are three NPCs in . They are three Tirkin chefs and members of the Fire Dragons along with their leader. They are first found at Olno's Mess Hall inside the Ardainian Battleship in the Indoline Praetorium and later at Bellyfull Canteen in the Empire of Mor Ardain during the DLC Quest Midnight Feasting upon installing the New Quests Pack 1 of the Expansion Pass.

The Fire Dragons Recipe is an Info Item in . It is obtained from the Head Fire Dragon at Bellyfull Canteen in the Empire of Mor Ardain during the DLC Quest Midnight Feasting. Once obtained, Pyra can cook Pyra's Baked Redfish.

The Famed Gourmet Chefs are two DLC Shops in . They are respectively run by the Head Fire Dragon and a Fire Dragons Member at the Bellyfull Canteen in the Empire of Mor Ardain during the DLC quest Midnight Feasting. They are specialized in Dishes.

Fadhail is an NPC in . He is an Ardainian soldier who can be found at Port Anangham in the Empire of Mor Ardain. He offers the Merc Mission Longing for Mòrag. He is one of the first characters to welcome the party to the Empire and gives a short verbal tour as he looks out to the horizon beyond the port.
Family vs. Fiends is a quest in . It can be received from Maryn and Terry in Torika Alley in Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya.
Failure and Success (Japanese: , Seihai) is a Blade Quest in . It is received from Ellenora at Nharil Central Plaza in the Empire of Mor Ardain.
Filias is an NPC in . He is an Ardainian who can be found at the Beraf Industry Ward in the Empire of Mor Ardain. He is spoken to during the quest Failure and Success.

Fact Bunnits (Japanese: , Fakuto Banitto) are Story Exclusive Enemy in . They are members of the Bunnit family, and can be found at level 26 - 30 in the Old Factory of the Empire of Mor Ardain during Chapter 4.

Fashion Show is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Uraya during the Blade Quest Bearing Her Soul, after Ursula's Looks reaches Level 9. The time required to complete this mission is 30 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 7 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Earth Mastery" and "Fire Mastery" Field Skills. It increases Ursula's fanbase by a large amount. This mission will become unobtainable if not unlocked before the end of the quest.
Fionnagh is an NPC in . She is an Ardainian who can be found at Seoris Plaza in the Indoline Praetorium.

Five Centuries of Memories is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is unlocked after resting at Aunt Corinne's House in Fonsett Village only after starting Chapter 9, and can be found in the Canyon of Husks in Spirit Crucible Elpys. __FORCETOC__

Family Ties is a Heart-to-Heart in . It can be found by the Morytha Falls in the Cliffs of Morytha after completing Chapter 7. The two options to choose between are Surely he'd be happy to see his big sis. and Sounds like you don't want to see him.... __FORCETOC__

Farm Riiks (Japanese: , Fāmu Ratōru) are Challenge Battle Enemies in . They are members of the Riik family, and are fought at level 30 during the fourth wave of the Challenge Battle, Pest Control. This enemy drops no items.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Fighter's Circlets (Japanese: , Tatakaumono no Kanmuri) are DLC accessories in and . They boost the wearer's resistance to the Doom debuff by up to 100%, allowing for full immunity to the status. They are the upgraded version of the Seven-League Circlet accessory. They can be found in the Land of Challenge from Treasure Troves obtained after completing a Challenge Battle, available as downloadable content from the Challenge Battle Mode Pack of the Expansion Pass.
Favyola is an NPC in . She is an Urayan, found in Fonsa Myma just above Briarley Trading.
